name: zenit-solar
description: Free CFE electricity tariff lookups and solar calculators for Mexico: current rates, estimated bills, solar system sizing, 25-year savings and battery (BESS) sizing. No account needed; results in Spanish and Mexican pesos.

interface.longDescription:
Zenit Solar answers everyday questions about electricity costs and solar power in Mexico with the same calculation engine Zenit's solar installers use for their quotes. No account or sign-up is needed, and results come back in Spanish, in Mexican pesos.

What it can do
• Current CFE rates for any tariff: residential 1, 1A–1F and DAC (summer and non-summer consumption blocks, DAC limit), low-tension PDBT, GDBT, RABT and APBT, medium-tension GDMTO, GDMTH, RAMT and APMT (including GDMTH base, intermediate and peak periods) and the 9-CU/9-N agricultural tariffs, as published by CFE, before VAT, with the publication month.
• Estimated CFE bill, month by month, for a given monthly consumption (kWh), including the summer/non-summer difference and a warning when consumption exceeds the DAC limit.
• Solar system sizing: how many panels and how many kW cover your consumption, using the solar yield of your region (NREL PVWatts data by CFE tariff region).
• 25-year savings projection with regional CFE rates and, when you give the system price, payback, IRR and NPV.
• Battery (BESS) sizing for peak shaving in businesses on GDMTH/GDMTO tariffs, verified with an hourly dispatch simulation.

How to use it
Tell it your consumption (monthly or bimonthly kWh, as printed on your CFE bill), your tariff (also on the bill) and your state. For example: «Consumo 300 kWh al mes en tarifa 1C en Mérida, ¿cuánto pagaría de luz?»

Limitations
All figures are estimates based on CFE's published tables and typical solar yields; they are not a quotation, an official bill or financial advice. The plugin cannot read your CFE account or your actual bill, covers only CFE tariffs in Mexico, and applies VAT at the general 16 % rate. CFE updates its rates monthly; the plugin refreshes them when they are published.
capabilities: Look up current CFE electricity rates by tariff and region
Estimate a CFE bill month by month from monthly kWh
Size a solar system (panels and kW) for a given consumption
Project 25-year solar savings, payback, IRR and NPV
Size a battery (BESS) for peak shaving on GDMTH/GDMTO tariffs
defaultPrompt: ¿Cuánto cuesta el kWh en la tarifa 1F en Hermosillo, Sonora, en julio?
Mi recibo bimestral de CFE es de 900 kWh en Guadalajara, ¿cuántos paneles solares necesito?
Gasto 6,000 kWh al año en tarifa DAC en Monterrey. Si el sistema cuesta $120,000, ¿en cuántos años se paga?

positive.description: Current rates for a residential tariff in a given month. Prompt (Spanish): «How much is a kWh on tariff 1F in Hermosillo, Sonora, in July?»
positive.prompt: ¿Cuánto cuesta el kWh en la tarifa 1F en Hermosillo, Sonora, en julio?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_cfe_tariff_rates with tariff 1F, state Sonora and month 7, without asking for anything else. Answers in Spanish with the four summer consumption blocks of 1F in MXN per kWh (July is in the 1F summer season, April to October): básico up to 300 kWh, intermedio bajo up to 1,200 kWh, intermedio alto up to 2,500 kWh and excedente above that; it also gives the DAC limit of 2,500 kWh per month, the month of CFE's publication and a note that prices are before VAT. Figures are presented as estimates from CFE's published tables; the exact prices change when CFE publishes a new month.

positive.description: Estimated monthly bill with the summer / non-summer difference. Prompt (Spanish): «I use 300 kWh a month on tariff 1C in Mérida, Yucatán. How much would I pay for electricity?»
positive.prompt: Consumo 300 kWh al mes en tarifa 1C en Mérida, Yucatán. ¿Cuánto pagaría de luz?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls calculate_cfe_bill with monthlyKwh 300, tariff 1C and state Yucatán. Answers with an estimated cost per month that shows the summer (April to October, roughly MXN 380) versus non-summer (roughly MXN 850) difference, the annual total (about MXN 6,900) and that VAT is included. No DAC warning, because 300 kWh is under the 1C limit. Amounts may differ slightly after CFE's monthly rate update.

positive.description: Solar system sizing from a bimonthly bill. Prompt (Spanish): «My bimonthly CFE bill is 900 kWh in Guadalajara, how many solar panels do I need?»
positive.prompt: Mi recibo bimestral de CFE es de 900 kWh en Guadalajara, ¿cuántos paneles solares necesito?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls calculate_system_size with bimonthlyKwh 900 and state Jalisco (Guadalajara is in Jalisco). Answers that the annual consumption is 5,400 kWh and recommends 7 panels of 550 W (about 3.85 kW) producing roughly 5,800 kWh per year for the sur region, labeled as an estimate.

positive.description: 25-year savings and payback with a known system price. Prompt (Spanish): «I use 6,000 kWh a year on the DAC tariff in Monterrey. If the system costs MXN 120,000, how much do I save and in how many years does it pay for itself?»
positive.prompt: Gasto 6,000 kWh al año en tarifa DAC en Monterrey. Si el sistema cuesta $120,000, ¿en cuántos años se paga?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls estimate_solar_savings with yearlyKwh 6000, tariff DAC, state Nuevo León and systemPriceMxn 120000; it may call calculate_system_size first with the same consumption and state (both return the same system). Answers with a 7-panel, about 3.85 kW system, first-year savings of about MXN 40,000 (about MXN 3,400 per month), 25-year savings of about MXN 1.67 million assuming 4 % annual rate escalation, a payback of about 2.8 years, an IRR of about 38 % and an NPV of about MXN 388,000, all labeled as estimates.

positive.description: Battery sizing for peak shaving on a medium-tension tariff. Prompt (Spanish): «I have a two-shift factory in Querétaro on tariff GDMTH using 240,000 kWh a year. What battery do I need to cut my peak demand by 20 %?»
positive.prompt: Tengo una fábrica de dos turnos en Querétaro con tarifa GDMTH que consume 240,000 kWh al año. ¿Qué batería necesito para bajar 20 % mi demanda máxima?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls calculate_bess_sizing with yearlyKwh 240000, tariff GDMTH, state Querétaro and targetPeakReductionPct 20 (the two-shift industrial load profile is the default). Answers with an estimated peak of about 42 kW, a target of about 34 kW and a battery of about 9 kW and 136 kWh nominal, and reports that the hourly dispatch simulation confirms the 20 % reduction is achievable. It states that the peak is estimated from a typical load profile, not from a metered bill.

negative.description: Out of scope: a utility outside Mexico. The plugin only covers CFE tariffs in Mexico, so no Zenit Solar tool should be called and a CFE estimate must never be presented as an Iberdrola bill. Expected: ChatGPT answers without the plugin, for example by explaining that the amount depends on the Iberdrola contract and asking for its tariff and contracted power. Prompt (Spanish): «How much will I pay for electricity this month in Madrid with Iberdrola if I used 300 kWh?»
negative.prompt: ¿Cuánto voy a pagar de luz este mes en Madrid con Iberdrola si consumí 300 kWh?

negative.description: Cannot access a real CFE account. The plugin has no access to CFE accounts, service numbers or actual bills; it only estimates from a consumption the user provides. Expected: ChatGPT explains this and offers an estimate if the user shares the monthly kWh and tariff from the bill, without calling a tool with an invented consumption. Prompt (Spanish): «Look up my CFE bill with service number 123456789012 and tell me how much I owe this month.»
negative.prompt: Consulta mi recibo de CFE con el número de servicio 123456789012 y dime cuánto debo este mes.

negative.description: No commerce or payments. The plugin sells nothing, hires no installers and processes no payments. Expected: ChatGPT declines the purchase and payment request (it may offer a savings estimate instead); no tool is expected to run. Prompt (Spanish): «Hire the installation of 7 panels for my house and charge the MXN 120,000 to my card.»
negative.prompt: Contrátame la instalación de 7 paneles para mi casa y cóbrame los $120,000 a mi tarjeta.

review.commerce_description: This plugin sells nothing and processes no payments. All five tools are free, read-only calculators; results link only to informational pages on zenitmaster.com, never to sign-up, pricing or checkout.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: CFE tariff lookup, estimated bill, solar system sizing, 25-year savings and battery (BESS) sizing for Mexico. All tools are free and read-only.

es-MX.subtitle: Tarifas CFE y ahorro solar
es-MX.description:
Zenit Solar responde las preguntas de todos los días sobre el costo de la luz y la energía solar en México con el mismo motor de cálculo que usan los instaladores solares de Zenit en sus cotizaciones. No requiere cuenta ni registro; los resultados se entregan en español y en pesos mexicanos.

Qué puede hacer
• Precios vigentes de CFE para cualquier tarifa: doméstica 1, 1A–1F y DAC (bloques de verano y fuera de verano, límite DAC), baja tensión PDBT, GDBT, RABT y APBT, media tensión GDMTO, GDMTH, RAMT y APMT (con los horarios base, intermedia y punta de GDMTH) y las tarifas agrícolas 9-CU/9-N, tal como las publica CFE, antes de IVA y con el mes de publicación.
• Recibo CFE estimado, mes por mes, para un consumo mensual dado (kWh), con la diferencia entre verano y fuera de verano y un aviso cuando el consumo rebasa el límite DAC.
• Dimensionamiento solar: cuántos paneles y cuántos kW cubren tu consumo, con el rendimiento solar de tu región (datos NREL PVWatts por región tarifaria CFE).
• Proyección de ahorro a 25 años con las tarifas CFE de tu región y, si indicas el precio del sistema, payback, TIR y VPN.
• Dimensionamiento de batería (BESS) para recorte de demanda (peak shaving) en negocios con tarifa GDMTH/GDMTO, verificado con una simulación de despacho horario.

Cómo usarlo
Indica tu consumo (kWh mensuales o bimestrales, como viene en el recibo), tu tarifa (también viene en el recibo) y tu estado. Por ejemplo: «Consumo 300 kWh al mes en tarifa 1C en Mérida, ¿cuánto pagaría de luz?»

Limitaciones
Todas las cifras son estimaciones basadas en las tablas publicadas por CFE y en rendimientos solares típicos; no son una cotización, un recibo oficial ni asesoría financiera. El plugin no puede leer tu cuenta de CFE ni tu recibo real, cubre únicamente las tarifas de CFE en México y aplica el IVA general del 16 %. CFE actualiza sus tarifas cada mes; el plugin las refresca cuando se publican.
